alternatives.argument: The local definition explicitly gives a complex vector space, complex-bilinear associative product, unit, conjugate-linear involution with (ab)*=b*a*, (a*)*=a and 1*=1, and a complex-linear functional normalized at 1 and nonnegative on every a*a. It assumes no norm or C*-completion.

Expand q(a+zb)=ω((a+zb)*(a+zb)) for z=1 and z=i to derive ω(a*b)=overline{ω(b*a)}. If q(b)>0 choose z=-overline{ω(a*b)}/q(b) to obtain |ω(a*b)|²≤q(a)q(b). If q(b)=0, a nonzero cross coefficient can be assigned a phase and arbitrarily large modulus to make q(a+zb)<0, so that coefficient is zero. Thus null vectors form the radical and a linear subspace. For a∈N and c∈A, apply the inequality to a and c*c a; it gives ω((ca)*(ca))=0, so N is a left ideal.

Cauchy–Schwarz makes ([a],[b])=ω(b*a) independent of representatives and positive definite on A/N. Under the exact Countable Choice hypothesis, apply the published Hilbert-completion theorem. Left multiplication π(a)[b]=[ab] is well defined by the left-ideal property and preserves products, unit and domain. The identity (π(a)[b],[c])=([b],π(a*)[c]) gives π(a)* restricted to D. If x_n→0 in D and π(a)x_n→y, then (y,z)=lim(x_n,π(a*)z)=0 for every dense-domain z, so y=0 and the graph closure is a graph. Ω=[1] is a cyclic unit vector recovering ω. For any second algebraically cyclic *-representation of the same state, [a]↦ρ(a)Ω′ is a well-defined dense-range isometry and extends uniquely to an intertwining unitary.

alternatives.argument: The local definition spells out all operations of a unital complex *-algebra and defines a state as a complex-linear functional ω with ω(1)=1 and ω(a*a) real and nonnegative for every a.

For q(a+zb)=ω((a+zb)*(a+zb)), positivity at z=1 and z=i gives the Hermitian identity. Completing the square proves the inequality when q(b)>0. When q(b)=0, any nonzero cross term can be made negative by choosing its phase and a sufficiently large modulus, so it must vanish. The resulting radical N is a subspace; applying the inequality to a and c*c a proves ca∈N.

Cauchy–Schwarz gives a well-defined positive inner product on A/N; Countable Choice is inherited exactly from the published completion supplier. The left ideal gives a well-defined common-domain representation by left multiplication. Its adjoint identity proves closability by the graph-sequence criterion, the unit class is cyclic and recovers ω, and equality of the state in a second cyclic *-representation defines an isometric intertwiner that extends to a unitary.
